Misdemeanors Attorney in Dubuque, IA: Quick Overview

A first- or second-offense OWI, or drug possession, in Dubuque, IA is classified as a misdemeanor under Iowa law. A conviction can still affect your license, your job, your housing, and your record for years.

Henkels & Baker, PC can review your charges, examine how the evidence was gathered, and work to protect your rights at every step — whether that means a reduced charge, a dismissal, a deferred judgment, or a strong defense at trial.

What a Misdemeanor OWI & Drug Charge Attorney in Dubuque, IA Can Do for Your Defense

If you’ve been charged with a first- or second-offense OWI, or with drug possession in Dubuque, IA, you’re probably unsure about what happens next. These charges may be classified as misdemeanors, but a conviction in Iowa can affect your license, your job, your housing, and your record for years.

The stakes are real — and so is the help available to you.

Henkels & Baker, PC serves people across Dubuque and the surrounding region who are facing OWI and drug charges. Our criminal defense work centers on these two areas, so the cases we see day to day are the cases you’re dealing with right now.

Iowa handles OWI and drug offenses under specific statutes with specific rules. A first-offense OWI is a serious misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 321J.2. First-offense possession of a controlled substance is a serious misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 124.401(5). Each carries its own penalties, license consequences, and possible paths to a better outcome — and the details of your stop, search, and arrest can change everything.

You don’t have to figure this out alone. We can review your charges, examine how the evidence was gathered, and work to protect your rights at every step — whether that means a reduced charge, a dismissal, a deferred judgment, or a strong defense at trial.

What a Misdemeanor OWI or Drug Conviction Can Cost You in Iowa

An OWI or drug charge is a serious legal matter, and the consequences can follow you long after the case ends. In Iowa, even a first offense can result in jail time, substantial fines, license consequences, and a criminal record that appears on background checks conducted by landlords, employers, and schools.

Here’s what Iowa law actually provides for the charges this firm handles:

  • First-offense OWI — serious misdemeanor (Iowa Code § 321J.2): A first OWI carries a minimum of 48 hours and up to one year in jail, a minimum fine of $1,250 (plus a 35% surcharge and court costs), and a driver’s license revocation of 180 days if you failed a chemical test or one year if you refused testing.

  • Second-offense OWI — aggravated misdemeanor (Iowa Code § 321J.2): A second OWI within twelve years carries a minimum of seven days and up to two years in jail, a fine of $1,875 to $6,250, and a longer license revocation.

  • First-offense drug possession — serious misdemeanor (Iowa Code § 124.401(5)): Possession of a controlled substance other than marijuana carries up to one year in jail and a fine of $430 to $2,560. First-offense marijuana possession carries up to six months in jail and/or a fine of up to $1,000.

The costs don’t stop at fines. A conviction can trigger mandatory substance abuse treatment, disqualify you from certain professional licenses, affect your ability to rent, and limit eligibility for federal student aid.

And with an OWI, the license consequences move on a separate track through the Iowa Department of Transportation — often before your criminal case is resolved.

Key Facts About Misdemeanor Charges in Dubuque

  • A first-offense OWI is a serious misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 321J.2.

  • A second-offense OWI within twelve years is an aggravated misdemeanor with heavier penalties.

  • First-offense drug possession is a serious misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 124.401(5).

  • OWI license consequences move on a separate track through the Iowa DOT.

  • Some Iowa misdemeanor convictions may later be eligible for expungement.

  • A Firm with Deep Iowa Roots: Henkels & Baker, PC has served clients in Iowa since 1973 and has represented people in criminal and traffic matters throughout eastern Iowa.

  • Free Consultation: The firm offers free consultations, so you can talk through your charges, ask hard questions, and understand your options before committing to anything.

Your Misdemeanor Case in Iowa — Step by Step

Once you move forward, your attorney digs into the details. That means reviewing the police report, arrest records, and any evidence tied to your case. Here is how the process typically unfolds from your first call to final resolution.

  • Step 1: Free Consultation: You share the basic facts — what you were charged with, when it happened, and any details about the arrest. You leave with a clear picture of your options, not more confusion.

  • Step 2: Case Review: Your attorney reviews the police report, arrest records, and any evidence tied to your case, looking for any issues with how evidence was gathered or how you were treated.

  • Step 3: Building a Strategy: Your attorney looks at the charge level, the strength of the evidence, and your personal history. From there, a strategy takes shape.

  • Step 4: Pretrial Hearings and Negotiations: Your attorney may attend pretrial hearings at the Dubuque County Courthouse and talk directly with the prosecutor to reduce the charge, lower the penalty, or reach a plea agreement.

  • Step 5: Trial — If It Comes to That: In Iowa, misdemeanor trials move faster than felony trials — many wrap up within one or two days.

  • Step 6: Sentencing or Dismissal: If the charge is reduced or dismissed, you may avoid fines and jail time entirely. In some Iowa cases, completing certain programs may allow you to seek an expungement later on.

Talk to a Misdemeanors Attorney in Dubuque, IA Today

An OWI or drug charge in Iowa is a serious matter that can affect your license, your job, your record, and your daily life — and the decisions you make right now can shape what happens next. You don’t have to face it alone.

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we work with people across Dubuque and the surrounding region to develop a clear, honest defense strategy tailored to their specific situation. We know the local courts and how Iowa’s OWI and drug processes work.

Your Next Step Is Simple

Your next step is simple. Reach out, tell us what happened, and let’s talk through your options together. We treat every client with respect and make sure you understand where you stand before any decision is made.

Contact us and schedule a free initial consultation.

1. Can a misdemeanor charge be expunged from my record in Iowa?

    2. Iowa law allows some misdemeanor convictions to be expunged, but timing and eligibility matter — you typically need to wait a set period after completing your sentence and have no new convictions. An attorney can review your record and tell you whether you qualify.

  2. What happens if I miss my court date for a misdemeanor in Iowa?

    3. If you miss a scheduled court date, the Dubuque County court may issue a bench warrant for your arrest. Contact a misdemeanor attorney right away; acting fast can sometimes help resolve the warrant before things get worse.

  3. Will a misdemeanor affect my ability to get a job in Iowa?

    4. Many Iowa employers run background checks, and a misdemeanor conviction can show up and create obstacles — especially in fields like healthcare, education, or finance. Keeping a conviction off your record, or minimizing the charge, may protect your job prospects.

  4. Does a misdemeanor conviction affect my driver’s license in Iowa?

    5. Certain misdemeanors — especially those tied to alcohol or reckless driving — can trigger a license suspension through the Iowa Department of Transportation. Your attorney can tell you whether your specific charge carries that risk.

  5. What if I were charged with a misdemeanor, but it’s my first offense?

    6. First-time offenders in Iowa may be eligible for deferred judgment or a similar outcome that avoids a permanent conviction on their record. Outcomes vary based on the charge, your history, and how your case is handled from the start.
